P1.evidence: The setter read-back is the best example in the batch and it did real work: three separate notes from Kim were used inside the first four minutes — 'I saw that Kim made a note of like something of skinny fat', 'he also mentioned something with having two terrorist rights, so two injuries that you've had' and 'I heard him mention something about your confidence levels at the moment'. Each one opened a line of discovery the prospect might not have volunteered. Against that, there was effectively no frame at all: 'Let's just dive into it and make the most use of our time together... taking it short, what can we potentially help you with?' No structure was set, no disqualification promise made and no agreement asked for.

P2.evidence: Age, weight and height asked in one clean question. Injuries pursued properly from the setter note — mechanism, which leg, when, whether surgery, how long the recovery, and what he can and cannot currently do. Current training established directly, and the results question was asked well: 'do you feel like you're gaining weight, gaining muscle at the moment, or is it just very stagnant?' Diet was the most detailed capture in the batch, including a check on whole versus processed and a sensible follow-up when 1,400-1,500 calories looked low for a six-foot man. The gaps: work was confirmed from notes rather than asked ('I think you're in FinTech, right?') and desk-bound versus active never established, health conditions never asked, and sleep never raised at all.

P3.evidence: The bridge ran well and produced the best material in the call: 'why is that not enough for you? There's so many people that are 40 out there like, I don't care, I'll just do it when I'm 50 or 60' drew out the CrossFit period, the mental sharpness and its link to his work. The reflect-back was delivered and was accurate — 'you don't have massive goals of you need to be the biggest father figure or something, no, for you it comes down to getting that fear out of your system' — correctly naming fear rather than fitness as the subject. But the phase stopped at the individual. 'Who else does that impact?' was never asked, and when the prospect said 'There is no goal, to be honest', the rep pushed once with 'well, it's important to have a goal, right?' and then let it go. Nothing about family, partner or children was ever established; we do not know from this transcript whether he has any.

P4.evidence: The most complete Past Attempts phase in the batch. What he had tried came out in full — daily CrossFit, self-built AI plans, approaches to personal trainers. What happened with each was pursued: the CrossFit class times against a 7am office start and an hour commute, the trainers who could only offer five or six o'clock. 'What has stopped you up until now to then look into doing something with it again?' produced the real answer, and 'Why haven't you done that yet?' about the local trainer closed the loop. He let the prospect name the gap in his own words: 'I require some kind of a hand-holding initially, then I'll be of my own.' Only P4f is missing, and it was unusually applicable — this is a man who used AI to write himself a perfectly good plan and cannot execute it, which is the exact case the line was written for.

P5.evidence: The consequence frame does not appear anywhere. He was never asked what the next two years look like if nothing changes, never asked whether he was willing to settle, never asked why not, and never asked to draw a line. This is the third call in the batch where the phase carrying 20 points of weight was skipped entirely, and here it is the most costly of the three: a man who has not trained in three years because he is afraid, and who ends the call at six or seven out of ten, was never once asked what another three years of that looks like.

P6.evidence: The belief question ran before the presentation — 'when it comes to making sure that you have the structure, that it fits into your schedule, and that it's just simple... if you have all of those things, would it then be a success for you?' — answered 'Yes, please.' A 1-10 gate ran after the pillars and returned an honest six or seven with the reason attached. The all-in question was never asked. Credit where it is due on P6c: he did not have a clear yes and he did not move forward anyway, which is what the script demands. What he did not do is the other half of the instruction — return to Phase 5 — which was unavailable because Phase 5 had never been run.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted and no price was ever named, so the phase was never reachable.

objection_plays.detail: Fear and doubt was not one objection among several here, it was the whole call — 'I'm scared, and I just need to get that scare out of me' and 'my phone may be super bad, and I injure myself right away'. Not one move from the play ran. No 'would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty?', no pleasure-versus-pain question, no bridge, no plane, no burned-before analogy, and above all no 'how will you know if you never actually try?', which was the natural close on a prospect who ended with 'I can give it a try'. The rep did engage the objection with his own material and it was reasonable material — light initial loads, form explained before the first repetition, video demonstrations to copy, others with the same injuries in the community — but he improvised where a play exists, and he finished with an absolute assurance rather than a reframe.

'Give me a day or two to think about it and then I'll circle back'. The isolation move ran and ran cleanly — he named the decision precisely, 'it only comes down to the aspect of someone in physical versus someone not', and the prospect confirmed it. Nothing else did: no can-it-get-you-there, no thinking-versus-deciding, no different-decision line, no identity move. He then granted the time explicitly ('I don't want you to make a bad decision for yourself') and set a return date. Given the prospect sat at six or seven, granting it was defensible; running none of the play was not.

Asynchronous delivery against a fear of physical harm. The prospect's objection was mechanical and specific: filming a movement and getting notes back tomorrow is an afterthought, and he could injure himself in the gap. 'It is an afterthought... and then I'm basically getting to the next day in order to figure out, like, okay, what exactly was my information... I'm just worried, like, it does not become too late, that I have tore something else again.' There is no scripted path for this, and it is distinct from the clinical-fit gap already logged from the Tyron Giuliani call — the programme is not contraindicated for him, the feedback loop is simply too slow for his risk tolerance.

AI and app substitutes. 'How is this different for me than just paying up an app with Nike or Ladder or something' and 'I use a lot of AI, and so I have created my own plan on what exactly I want to do'. This is a variant of the cheaper-substitute gap but the substitute is a piece of software rather than a person, and it is worth logging separately because the differentiator the rep needed — that an app cannot see whether your knee is tracking — is exactly the point the prospect was already disputing about video review. The rep's reply was to replay the history back at him, which is sound but is not a play.

notes: Discovery was the strongest in the batch — Phase 4 ran almost complete, the setter notes were used three times in four minutes, and the reflect-back correctly identified fear rather than fitness as the subject. Two gaps decided it. Phase 5 was absent, so a man who has been stuck for three years was never made to picture a fourth. And the single objection the entire call turned on was a textbook fear-and-doubt trigger with a written play behind it, and none of that play ran; it was answered with reassurance, ending in an absolute safety claim to a prospect whose stated worry is being injured.
